meta.title: AMDL: Apple Music to your own disk, lossless and tagged
meta.description: AMDL is a self-hosted, open-source downloader. Paste an Apple Music link or search the catalog, and it saves finished, tagged .m4a files: ALAC up to 24-bit/192 kHz, Dolby Atmos or AAC. Use it from a web console, a terminal, or an AI agent over MCP.
meta.ogAlt: AMDL: Apple Music, on your own disk.

hero.title:
Apple Music,
on your own disk.
hero.subtitle: Lossless, tagged.
hero.lead: Paste a song, album, playlist, artist or station link, or search the catalog. AMDL downloads, decrypts, remuxes and tags every track into a finished `.m4a`: ALAC up to 24-bit/192 kHz, Dolby Atmos or AAC.

stats.label: Kinds of link, song to station

how.title: From a link to a finished file.
how.lead: By default, when one codec runs out of attempts, the next one on your list takes over, with AAC-LC as the last resort.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.text: Reads the song, album, playlist, artist or station behind the link from Apple's catalog, with each track's metadata.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Fetches the encrypted segments from Apple's CDN and retries with backoff.

steps.title: Decrypt
steps.text: In process, in pure Go. Your wrapper supplies a key template; AMDL itself holds no Apple account and no keys.

steps.title: Remux
steps.text: Decrypted samples go straight into ffmpeg, so no plaintext copy of the whole track is written to disk.

steps.title: Tag
steps.text: Verifies the file, then writes the metadata, artwork and lyrics.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Moves the finished file to the path your template gives it. A file that is already there is skipped, unless you ask for it to be overwritten.

products.title: One core, four ways in.
products.lead: Every product runs on the same Go core. Deploy the server once, then use whichever fits the moment.

server.label: Server
server.name: amdl serve
server.text: The backend you deploy: one Go process with a SQLite database, a REST and Server-Sent Events API under `/api/v1`, and the web console on the same port. Images for amd64 and arm64 are on GHCR.
points: Jobs survive a restart and pick up where they stopped.
Downloads, decryption and wrapper calls share process-wide pools.
No accounts or auth, on purpose: put a reverse proxy in front.

console.label: Web console
console.name: Web console
console.text: The browser client, embedded in the server at `/console/`. Search the catalog or paste links, watch each track move through its stages, and browse what you saved in each album's own colors.
points: A live queue with per-track stages and an album progress bar
Apple's animated covers, where an album has one
Logs, and status and settings on one page, on desktop and phone

shots.overview: The console's overview, on made-up data: the health line, three jobs running in the live queue, the latest finished album and a wall of covers
shots.drawer: A finished album's drawer over the queue, in the album's colors: the progress bar and every track with its length and size
shots.search: New download: catalog search results for Mira Lune, a made-up artist, with each song's audio formats
shots.phone: A finished album's drawer on a phone

terminal.label: Terminal
terminal.name: CLI · MCP · TUI
terminal.text: `amdl` is one binary with three faces. Scripts and agents get JSON on stdout and an exit status for each kind of failure. `amdl mcp` serves the same commands as MCP tools. And `amdl` on its own opens an interactive interface: paste a link, or type and press enter to search.
points: Renders inline, so finished jobs stay in your terminal's scrollback.
One card per running job, colored after its album artwork.
No server of your own? `amdl service install` runs the backend on this machine as a background service that starts at login.
terminal.shot: amdl's terminal interface: a job card with the album progress bar and per-track stage bars, a list of search results, the prompt and a status line

desktop.label: Desktop
desktop.name: Desktop app
desktop.text: A native app for macOS, Windows and Linux, drawn with MyGo's native UI. It works as a client of your server, or runs the pipeline itself and talks to a remote wrapper, sharing one backend and one download history with the command line. It ships with 2.0. The packages are not signed yet, so each system asks once before opening it: [installing the desktop app]({blob}/docs/install.md#the-desktop-app).

features.title: The parts you would otherwise script.

items.title: Codec fallback
items.text: List codecs in order: ALAC, Dolby Atmos, AAC and more. Each gets its own retry budget before the next one takes over.

items.title: Lyrics
items.text: Embedded as LRC, timed by line or by word, with translation and romanization if you want them. `.lrc` and `.ttml` files next to the track, too.

items.title: Animated covers
items.text: Apple's motion artwork plays in the console when an album has it. Looking it up never holds up a download.

items.title: Library sync
items.text: Watches your Apple Music library and downloads the album behind each song you add.

items.title: Job hooks
items.text: Call a webhook or run a command when a job is queued or ends, for example to refresh your media server.

items.title: Your folder layout
items.text: Path templates for songs, albums, artists, playlists and stations, built from variables such as `{ArtistName}` and `{AlbumName}`.

quickStart.title: Up and running in a few minutes.
quickStart.lead: You need an Apple Music subscription and a wrapper: the service that holds your Apple Music login. Run the wrapper on a Linux box, or let amdl run it in a QEMU guest on your own machine.

steps.title: Install amdl
steps.text: The script checks the release against its `SHA256SUMS` and puts `amdl` in `~/.local/bin`, printing the line to add to `PATH` if that folder is not on it. On Windows it goes to your user programs folder.

steps.title: Check ffmpeg
steps.text: Every track goes through ffmpeg. `amdl doctor` says whether this machine has it, and prints the command that installs it if not.

steps.title: Get a wrapper
steps.text: This downloads upstream's wrapper guest and checks it against a pinned hash; it needs QEMU, which it offers to install. Already run a wrapper on a NAS or server? Skip this step.

steps.title: Run the backend
steps.text: This registers the backend as a service that starts at login, and it starts the wrapper with it. For a wrapper elsewhere, add `--wrapper <its address>`. `amdl service status` prints the console's address: sign in on its Account page, or here with `amdl wrapper login`.

steps.title: Get the Compose file
steps.text: In an empty directory. Create `data/downloads` first and give it to the backend's user (`PUID:PGID`, 1000:1000 unless you set them); otherwise Docker creates it as root. The first start adds `configs/` and the rest of `data/`.

steps.title: Turn on the wrapper
steps.text: In `docker-compose.yml`, uncomment the `wrapper-manager` service and the `volumes:` block at the end of the file, then set the wrapper address:

steps.title: Start both
steps.text: Compose builds wrapper-manager from its v2 branch, so the host needs internet access.

steps.title: Sign in and download
steps.text: Open `http://localhost:18080/`, go to **Settings › Account** and sign in with your Apple ID. Paste a link into **New download**; finished files land in `./data/downloads`.

nas.label: NAS
nas.text: The wrapper needs user namespaces: `unshare -Ur true` must succeed. On a host without them, such as Synology DSM, use wrapper-manager v2's QEMU variant, which needs `/dev/kvm`.

quickStart.more: Every option of both paths is in the [install guide]({blob}/docs/install.md) and the [deployment guide]({blob}/docs/deployment.md).

agents.title: Made for agents to drive.
agents.lead: Every result is JSON on stdout, and every error a JSON object on stderr with an exit status for each kind of failure. `amdl cli search` finds the command for a task, `--dry-run` prints a change instead of sending it, and a destructive command asks first, or needs `--yes` outside a terminal.
agents.mcpNote: `amdl cli setup` prints everything a coding agent needs to connect and changes no files: the `claude mcp add` command, a Codex `config.toml` entry, an `mcpServers` entry, a paragraph for `AGENTS.md` and an agent skill. From a search to a download then takes two calls, `search_catalog` and `start_download`, and `wait_for_job` reports the album's progress while it waits. No tool signs the wrapper in, so a password never passes through a model.
agents.install: Releases attach `amdl` for Linux, macOS and Windows, and the server image ships it at `/app/amdl`.

notice.label: Notice
notice.text: AMDL needs your own Apple Music subscription and is for personal use: each install serves one person. It relies on Apple's undocumented web-player API, which can change without notice.
